newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sets barley refund of zero Ecus.
newsitem.headline: EU sets barley refund of zero Ecus.

text.p: The European Union on Thursday set a standing daily refund of zero Ecus on barley exports to third countries, a category which excludes exports to Switzerland and Liechtenstein, EU officials said.
The change, from a previous entry of "nil value," will ease the delivery of barley needed to complete contracts with Middle Eastern buyers in July and had been lobbied for by the trade.

A zero refund, while still offering no subsidy, is safer than a nil-value licence because prefixing is allowed. It also has full licence validity of up to five months and comes with normal monthly storage bonuses.
Officials confirmed the EU had also posted a standing refund of five Ecus on barley exports to Switzerland and Liechtenstein.
Its cereals management committee also set a daily refund of 13 Ecus per tonne on rye exports to the same countries and one Ecu on wheat flour exports to any destination.
Standing refunds are drawn through the EU's daily export channel, which usually has no volume constraints but is subject to a three-day veto by the European Commission.
The system is an alternative to the refunds handed out at the EU's main weekly tender, which depend on traders' bids.
